question: Which correctly describes chiplets?
choices: A technology that connects several small chips, divided by function, inside one package so they operate as one system
A technology that uses an entire wafer as a single chip
A technology that solders chips directly to the board without a package
explanation: Instead of putting every function on one large chip, the chiplet approach makes the compute section, I/O section and so on as separate small chips and connects them at high density inside a package. Small chips have high yield, and the best manufacturing process can be chosen for each function.

question: Which correctly describes a TSV (through-silicon via)?
choices: Lateral wiring formed only on the chip surface
An electrode that passes through the silicon substrate in the thickness direction, connecting stacked chips vertically
A solder ball used as an external package terminal
explanation: A TSV (Through-Silicon Via) is an electrode made by drilling a hole in the silicon substrate and filling it with conductor, electrically connecting the front and back of the substrate. It allows chips to be stacked with many connections over shorter distances than wire bonding, so it is used in 3D packaging and HBM.

question: Which correctly describes HBM (High Bandwidth Memory)?
choices: A slow memory using a single layer of flash memory
An SRAM cache built into the CPU chip
A memory that stacks several DRAM dies with TSVs and achieves high bandwidth with a very wide bus
explanation: HBM stacks several DRAM dies with TSVs and connects them to the processor through a very wide data bus of more than 1,000 lines, achieving high data transfer bandwidth. It is used in 2.5D packaging, placed beside the processor on a silicon interposer or similar, and is mounted on AI GPUs and other devices.

question: Which correctly describes the role of the silicon interposer used in 2.5D packaging?
choices: A heat sink for cooling chips
An intermediate substrate on which several chips are placed side by side and connected at high density with fine wiring
explanation: A silicon interposer is an intermediate silicon substrate with fine wiring made by semiconductor processes. Several chips, such as a processor and HBM, are placed side by side on it and connected with high-density wiring impossible on ordinary package substrates. The interposer connects to the package substrate through TSVs.

question: Which correctly describes hybrid bonding?
choices: A technology that enlarges solder bumps to improve connection reliability
A technology that connects using two wires at a time
A technology that directly bonds surfaces of copper electrodes and dielectric without bumps, enabling extremely dense connections
explanation: Hybrid bonding planarizes chip or wafer surfaces and directly bonds copper electrodes to each other and dielectric to dielectric at the same time. Because no solder bumps are used, connection pitch can be reduced to a few µm, and it is used in stacked image sensors and advanced chip stacking.

question: Which correctly describes a feature of fan-out wafer-level packaging (FOWLP)?
choices: Redistribution layers extend beyond the chip edges, so external terminals can be placed over an area larger than the chip
Connections are made only by wire bonding
The package is always smaller than the chip
explanation: In FOWLP, singulated chips are embedded in resin to form a reconstituted wafer, and redistribution layers extending beyond the chip edges are formed on it. It is thin without a substrate and can place many terminals, so it has been adopted for smartphone processors and similar devices.

question: Which industry-standard die-to-die interface aims to let chiplets from different companies connect to each other?
explanation: UCIe (Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express) is a standard for connecting chiplets within a package. A common standard makes it easier to combine chiplets made by different companies and on different processes, and is expected to broaden the use of chiplets.

question: Which is especially likely to be a challenge in 3D packaging, which stacks chips vertically?
choices: Chips are too light to secure
Temperature rise from heat generated by stacked chips, and removing that heat
explanation: 3D packaging has the advantage of shorter wiring, but because heat-generating chips are stacked, heat tends to build up and is hard to remove from the inner chips. Higher temperatures degrade performance and reliability, so thermal design is an important challenge.

question: Which correctly describes SiP (system in package)?
choices: Several chips and passive components are housed in one package to function as a system
All functions are integrated on one chip
A system is built with software alone
explanation: SiP builds a processor, memory, passive components and so on into one package to function as one system. Compared with an SoC, which integrates everything on one chip, it makes it easier to combine parts from different processes and can shorten development time.

question: In flip-chip connections, what is the main advantage of using copper pillars (Cu pillars) instead of solder balls?
choices: Bumps can be made larger to increase contact area
Bump pitch can be narrowed, and electrical and thermal conduction are also excellent
explanation: A Cu pillar bump is a copper pillar with a small amount of solder on its tip. Unlike solder balls, it does not melt and spread sideways, so the bump spacing (pitch) can be narrowed and many terminals placed. Copper conducts electricity and heat well, which also helps current capacity and heat dissipation.

question: What is the wiring layer called that is formed on a chip or wafer surface to route electrode positions to the positions of external terminals?
explanation: A redistribution layer (RDL) routes wiring from the chip's bond pads to where external terminals such as solder balls are to be placed. It is used in wafer-level packages, fan-out packages, interposers and more, and its wiring is becoming ever finer.

question: Which approach, instead of a large silicon interposer, embeds small pieces of silicon only at the chip-to-chip connection areas to achieve high-density wiring?
explanation: In the silicon bridge approach, small pieces of silicon covering only the connection areas between adjacent chips are embedded in the package substrate, and fine wiring on them connects the chips at high density. Because no large interposer is needed, large-area packaging becomes possible while keeping costs down.

question: Which is a correct advantage of glass substrates, being considered in place of organic materials for next-generation large package substrates?
choices: They are soft and easy to bend
They have high flatness and dimensional stability, making fine wiring easier to form
explanation: Glass has a flat surface and little dimensional change or warpage with temperature, so it is expected to make it easier to form fine wiring and dense through-vias even in large package substrates. Its application to large packages for AI and similar uses is being considered.

question: What is the technology called that mounts optical transceiver components close to switch ICs and the like in the same package, shortening electrical wiring to reduce power?
explanation: In data centers, as traffic grows, the power needed to transmit electrical signals over long distances has become a problem. CPO places optical transceiver components in the same package as switch ICs and the like, shortening the distance signals travel electrically and reducing power. It is one of the technologies integrating photonics and electronics.

question: Among hybrid bonding methods, which allows only chips judged good in test to be selected and bonded to the target wafer?
explanation: W2W bonding bonds entire wafers at once and is efficient, but defective chips get bonded to each other, and good chips to defective ones. C2W bonding can select and bond only good singulated chips, giving a yield advantage, and chips of different sizes can be combined.

question: What are the bumps called, far smaller than ordinary solder balls, used to connect chips stacked with TSVs and to connect chips to interposers?
explanation: Microbumps are very small bumps arranged at pitches of a few tens of µm, used for the many connections between chips. They are used to stack HBM DRAM dies and to connect chips on interposers. When an even finer pitch is needed, hybrid bonding is used.

question: In AI GPUs, what is the main reason the GPU chip and HBM are placed side by side on one silicon interposer?
choices: To connect the chips over short distances with an extremely large number of wires, achieving very high memory bandwidth
explanation: HBM has more than 1,000 data lines, too many to route on an ordinary package substrate. Placing the GPU and HBM side by side on a silicon interposer, where fine wiring can be made, connects them over short distances with many wires, achieving the very high memory bandwidth AI computation needs.

question: In 3D NAND, which is a correct advantage of making the memory cell array and peripheral circuits on separate wafers and bonding them together?
choices: The manufacturing process always takes just one step
Each can be made with a process suited to it, and chip area can be reduced
explanation: Making the memory cell array and peripheral (CMOS) circuits on separate wafers with optimal processes and bonding them together puts the peripheral circuits under the memory cells, reducing chip area. Another advantage is that the peripheral circuits are not affected by the cell array's high-temperature steps.

question: What is the material called that is placed between a chip and a heat spreader to fill microscopic gaps and improve heat transfer?
explanation: Even when solids are stacked together, microscopic surface roughness leaves gaps that make heat hard to transfer. A TIM (Thermal Interface Material) fills these gaps to improve heat transfer; types include greases, sheets and metal-based materials. It is an important component for high-power processors.

question: What is the data transfer capacity that can be secured per unit length of chip edge called, emphasized as a performance metric for chiplet interconnects?
choices: Bandwidth density (transfer rate per unit length of chip edge)
explanation: Chiplets are usually connected through terminals arranged along their edges, so how much data can be transferred per 1 mm of edge length (bandwidth density) is an important metric. The energy needed to send one bit is also emphasized.

question: Which correctly describes the difference between 2.5D and 3D packaging?
choices: 2.5D places chips side by side on an intermediate substrate (such as an interposer), while 3D stacks chips vertically
2.5D stacks chips vertically, while 3D places chips side by side
There is no difference between 2.5D and 3D
explanation: 2.5D packaging places several chips side by side on an intermediate substrate such as a silicon interposer and connects them through the substrate's fine wiring. 3D packaging stacks chips vertically and connects them with TSVs or hybrid bonding. Structures combining the two are also used.

question: In HBM, what is the typical number of DRAM dies stacked in one stack?
explanation: In HBM, DRAM dies connected with TSVs are stacked 8, 12 or even 16 high and combined with a base die (logic die) at the bottom to form one stack. More layers increase capacity, but techniques for thinning dies and countermeasures for heat become necessary.

question: What is the concept called that integrates chips made with different manufacturing processes and materials into one package?
explanation: Heterogeneous integration uses advanced packaging to integrate chips made with different processes and materials — advanced-process logic, DRAM, analog, RF, photonic devices and more — into one system. It is attracting attention as a way to overcome the limits of monolithic integration, which builds everything on one chip.

question: Which correctly describes the typical TSV formation process?
choices: Form it simply by pouring in solder
Etch a hole by deep etching, form an insulating film and barrier layer, then fill with copper or similar
explanation: A TSV is made by etching a hole in silicon by deep etching (such as the Bosch process), forming an insulating film, barrier layer and seed layer on the inside of the hole, then filling it with copper or similar by plating. The wafer is then thinned from the back to expose the TSV tips.

question: What is the main aim of manufacturing packages all at once on large rectangular panels instead of round wafers?
choices: To increase the number processed at once and improve area utilization, lowering cost
explanation: Rectangular panels can hold square packages with less waste than round wafers and are easier to scale up, so many packages can be processed at once. Panel-level packaging is being developed as a way to lower costs, for fan-out packages and others.

question: To stack chips with TSVs, approximately how thin are wafers ground from the back?
explanation: Chips stacked with TSVs are thinned to a few tens of µm to keep hole depth down and reduce the total thickness after stacking. Thin wafers crack and warp easily, so techniques such as temporarily bonding them to a carrier substrate for processing are used.

question: Which correctly describes the benefits expected from using chiplets?
choices: They always become cheaper and faster in every case
The best process can be chosen for each function, small chips raise yield, and designs are easier to reuse
explanation: With chiplets, the best process can be chosen for each function — for example, an advanced process for parts that need high performance and a mature process for I/O and analog. Small chips have high yield, and the same chiplet can be reused in multiple products. On the other hand, chip-to-chip interconnect and packaging costs are added.

question: Which correctly describes the conditions required of the surfaces to be joined in hybrid bonding?
choices: Very high flatness and cleanliness at the nanometer level
A thick oil film on the surface
explanation: Because hybrid bonding directly joins surfaces of copper electrodes and dielectric without bumps, the bonding surfaces must be flat at the nanometer level and free of particles and contamination. Even a tiny particle can cause unbonded cavities (voids). CMP and cleaning technologies are important.

question: Which correctly describes the role of the base die (logic die) at the bottom of an HBM stack?
choices: It handles the interface between the stacked DRAM and the processor, as well as functions such as test
explanation: The HBM base die handles signal exchange between the stacked DRAM dies and the processor and also includes circuits for test and repair. Recently there has also been a move to make the base die with a logic process and give it more functions.

question: For high-power AI packages, which is a correct example of cooling methods being considered and introduced?
choices: Do nothing and wait for natural cooling
Liquid cooling, such as flowing liquid through cold plates or immersion cooling
explanation: AI GPUs and similar devices consume from several hundred W to more than 1 kW per package, so air cooling can no longer remove all the heat. Methods such as flowing coolant through cold plates and immersion cooling, which submerges entire servers in dielectric liquid, are being introduced.
